reading.body:
Digital Realty's DFW28 facility in Richardson totals 121,500 square feet and reports 2N+1 cooling redundancy, a specification that qualifies it to host workloads with strict availability requirements. No power capacity is published for this building. Across Texas, 133 data center facilities are mapped and only 18 publish power figures; this facility ranks 19th among those with disclosed megawatt capacity, suggesting its published MW falls below the state's mapped portfolio, which totals 468 MW.

The absence of a published power figure is the binding constraint on interpreting this site's AI relevance. The facility's size and redundancy tier indicate it is designed for mission-critical compute, but without a wattage disclosure, the campus cannot be ranked against competing locations or assessed for its contribution to the state's AI infrastructure buildout. Digital Reality operates at least three other named facilities in Richardson on the same campus cluster; whether DFW28 is one building or a reference identifier spanning multiple structures is not clarified in the published specs.

For a decision-maker evaluating whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the missing power figure is decisive. Texas accounts for one of the largest published data center power bases in the US, yet the state's mapped facilities outnumber those with disclosed capacity by more than 7 to 1. Until operators publish wattage, this building remains a physical asset whose role in the grid constraint on AI compute cannot be quantified.
